title: Relative clauses 3
use_hint: Fix the sentence · Enter = check · Enter = next
note: B2 grammar unit, drafted 2026-09-05 on the home lane, replacing the empty shell. 30 items, inside the 24-40 band. Two predecessors own the basics and neither is repeated: b1_relative_clauses (66) has who/which/that plus where/when/why, defining clauses and the omission rule, and b1_relative_clauses_2 (25) has THE COMMA RULE — its own note calls that the single biggest Czech interference target at B1. Nothing here re-teaches either. Three genuinely new things, each a real B2 gap: **whose** (possession, and it works for things as well as people, which learners do not expect), **whom** after a preposition, and **which** pointing back at a WHOLE CLAUSE — *He arrived late, which annoyed everyone* — where Czech *což* comes out as *what* almost every time. The third block drills the everyday alternative to *to whom*: the preposition stranded at the END, which is what people actually say and what Czech word order makes impossible to guess. gap_class is genuinely useful on this unit and is used properly: **relative** on the 18 pronoun items, **preposition** on the 6 stranded-preposition items. That is the first unit on this lane where the two classes both apply. Distractors carry the unit's own errors (B4): *who's* against *whose*, *what* against sentence-*which*, *who* against *whom*, and *that* after a comma — all four are the Use stage as well. A8 accepts generated as a contraction closure; D1 every item names its own pronoun and why.

cards.title: Relative clauses 3
points: Three things the earlier units left out.
**whose** for possession · **whom** after a preposition · **which** for a whole idea.

rows: The man **whose** car was stolen called the police.
The person to **whom** I spoke was helpful.
That is the man I told you **about**.

cards.title: You already know
points: Relative clauses 1 gave you who, which, that, where, when and why.
Relative clauses 2 gave you the comma rule.
Everything here sits on top of both.

rows: The man **who** called is my boss.
My brother, **who** lives in Brno, is a doctor.

cards.title: whose
points: It works for things and organisations, not only people.
*Who's* is *who is* and has nothing to do with it.

cards.title: whom, and the everyday version
points: After a preposition, the form is **whom**.
In speech people move the preposition to the **end** and drop the pronoun.
Both are correct. The second is far commoner.

rows: the man for **whom** it was booked

cards.title: which for a whole idea
points: Here **which** does not point at a noun. It points at everything before the comma.

items.en: The man whose car was stolen called the police.
items.cz: Muž, kterému ukradli auto, zavolal policii.
items.gap: The man ____ car was stolen called the police.
accepts: The man whose car was stolen called the police.
items.explanation: **whose** shows possession — the car belongs to the man.
items.explanation_cz: **whose** ukazuje vlastnictví — auto patří tomu muži.

items.en: I met a woman whose son teaches at my school.
items.cz: Potkal jsem ženu, jejíž syn učí na mé škole.
items.gap: I met a woman ____ son teaches at my school.
accepts: I met a woman whose son teaches at my school.
items.explanation: **whose** + noun. *Who* cannot be followed by a noun like this.
items.explanation_cz: **whose** + podstatné jméno. *Who* takhle podstatné jméno mít nemůže.

items.en: The company whose name we forgot has closed.
items.cz: Firma, jejíž jméno jsme zapomněli, zavřela.
items.gap: The company ____ name we forgot has closed.
accepts: The company whose name we forgot has closed.
items.explanation: **whose** works for things as well as people.
items.explanation_cz: **whose** funguje pro věci stejně jako pro lidi.

items.en: She has a friend whose parents live in Berlin.
items.cz: Má kamarádku, jejíž rodiče žijí v Berlíně.
items.gap: She has a friend ____ parents live in Berlin.
accepts: She's a friend whose parents live in Berlin.
She is a friend whose parents live in Berlin.
She has a friend whose parents live in Berlin.
items.explanation: **whose** parents — the parents belong to the friend.
items.explanation_cz: **whose** parents — rodiče patří té kamarádce.

items.en: The student whose work you praised is here.
items.cz: Student, jehož práci jsi chválil, je tady.
items.gap: The student ____ work you praised is here.
accepts: The student whose work you praised is here.
items.explanation: **whose** work — possession again, and the clause is defining, so no commas.
items.explanation_cz: **whose** work — zase vlastnictví, a věta je určující, takže bez čárek.

items.en: That is the family whose house we bought.
items.cz: To je rodina, jejíž dům jsme koupili.
items.gap: That is the family ____ house we bought.
accepts: That's the family whose house we bought.
That is the family whose house we bought.
items.explanation: **whose** house. The house belongs to the family.
items.explanation_cz: **whose** house. Dům patří té rodině.

items.en: The person to whom I spoke was very helpful.
items.cz: Člověk, se kterým jsem mluvil, byl velmi ochotný.
items.gap: The person to ____ I spoke was very helpful.
accepts: The person to whom I spoke was very helpful.
items.explanation: After a preposition English uses **whom**, not *who*.
items.explanation_cz: Po předložce angličtina používá **whom**, ne *who*.

items.en: The colleague with whom she works is leaving.
items.cz: Kolega, se kterým pracuje, odchází.
items.gap: The colleague with ____ she works is leaving.
accepts: The colleague with whom she works is leaving.
items.explanation: *with* + **whom**. This is the formal pattern.
items.explanation_cz: *with* + **whom**. Tohle je formální vzorec.

items.en: The doctor from whom we got the letter has left.
items.cz: Lékař, od kterého jsme dostali ten dopis, odešel.
items.gap: The doctor from ____ we got the letter has left.
accepts: The doctor from whom we got the letter has left.
items.explanation: *from* + **whom** — the preposition forces *whom*.
items.explanation_cz: *from* + **whom** — předložka vynucuje *whom*.

items.en: He is the man for whom the room was booked.
items.cz: To je ten muž, pro kterého byl ten pokoj rezervovaný.
items.gap: He is the man for ____ the room was booked.
accepts: He's the man for whom the room was booked.
He is the man for whom the room was booked.
He has the man for whom the room was booked.
items.explanation: *for* + **whom**. Never *for who*.
items.explanation_cz: *for* + **whom**. Nikdy *for who*.

items.en: The friends with whom I travelled are here.
items.cz: Přátelé, se kterými jsem cestoval, jsou tady.
items.gap: The friends with ____ I travelled are here.
accepts: The friends with whom I travelled are here.
items.explanation: **whom** works for plural people too.
items.explanation_cz: **whom** funguje i pro víc lidí.

items.en: The writer about whom she wrote is now famous.
items.cz: Spisovatel, o kterém psala, je teď slavný.
items.gap: The writer about ____ she wrote is now famous.
accepts: The writer about whom she wrote is now famous.
items.explanation: *about* + **whom**. The preposition sits before it.
items.explanation_cz: *about* + **whom**. Předložka je před ním.

items.en: He arrived very late, which annoyed everyone.
items.cz: Přišel hodně pozdě, což všechny naštvalo.
items.gap: He arrived very late, ____ annoyed everyone.
accepts: He arrived very late, which annoyed everyone.
items.explanation: **which** can point back at the WHOLE sentence, not just one noun. Czech *což* is often written as *what* — it is always **which**.
items.explanation_cz: **which** může ukazovat zpět na CELOU větu, ne jen na jedno podstatné jméno. České *což* se často píše jako *what* — je to vždy **which**.

items.en: She passed the exam, which surprised nobody.
items.cz: Udělala tu zkoušku, což nikoho nepřekvapilo.
items.gap: She passed the exam, ____ surprised nobody.
accepts: She passed the exam, which surprised nobody.
items.explanation: **which** again for the whole idea. *That* cannot follow a comma.
items.explanation_cz: **which** zase pro celou myšlenku. *That* nemůže být po čárce.

items.en: They cancelled the trip, which cost us money.
items.cz: Zrušili ten výlet, což nás stálo peníze.
items.gap: They cancelled the trip, ____ cost us money.
accepts: They cancelled the trip, which cost us money.
items.explanation: The cancelling cost the money, so **which** points at the whole clause.
items.explanation_cz: Peníze stálo to zrušení, takže **which** ukazuje na celou větu.

items.en: He never answers emails, which is very rude.
items.cz: Nikdy neodpovídá na e-maily, což je velmi neslušné.
items.gap: He never answers emails, ____ is very rude.
accepts: He never answers emails, which is very rude.
items.explanation: **which** = the fact that he never answers.
items.explanation_cz: **which** = ten fakt, že nikdy neodpovídá.

items.en: The film ended at midnight, which was too late.
items.cz: Ten film skončil o půlnoci, což bylo moc pozdě.
items.gap: The film ended at midnight, ____ was too late.
accepts: The film ended at midnight, which was too late.
items.explanation: **which** covers the ending time, the whole situation.
items.explanation_cz: **which** pokrývá tu dobu konce, celou situaci.

items.en: She speaks four languages, which helps at work.
items.cz: Mluví čtyřmi jazyky, což pomáhá v práci.
items.gap: She speaks four languages, ____ helps at work.
accepts: She speaks four languages, which helps at work.
items.explanation: **which** for the whole ability, not for *languages* alone.
items.explanation_cz: **which** pro celou tu schopnost, ne jen pro *languages*.

items.en: That is the man I told you about.
items.cz: To je ten muž, o kterém jsem ti říkal.
items.gap: That is the man I told you ____.
accepts: That's the man I told you about.
That is the man I told you about.
items.explanation: In everyday English the preposition goes to the **end**: *told you about*.
items.explanation_cz: V běžné angličtině jde předložka na **konec**: *told you about*.

items.en: This is the house we used to live in.
items.cz: To je dům, ve kterém jsme bydleli.
items.gap: This is the house we used to live ____.
accepts: This is the house we used to live in.
items.explanation: *live in* a house — the preposition stays with the verb and moves to the end.
items.explanation_cz: *live in* a house — předložka zůstává u slovesa a jde na konec.

items.en: She is the person I was waiting for.
items.cz: To je ta osoba, na kterou jsem čekal.
items.gap: She is the person I was waiting ____.
accepts: She's the person I was waiting for.
She is the person I was waiting for.
She has the person I was waiting for.
items.explanation: *wait for* someone. The preposition never disappears.
items.explanation_cz: *wait for* někoho. Předložka nikdy nezmizí.

items.en: That is the club he belongs to.
items.cz: To je klub, do kterého patří.
items.gap: That is the club he belongs ____.
accepts: That's the club he belongs to.
That is the club he belongs to.
items.explanation: *belong to* — a fixed pair, and *to* lands at the end.
items.explanation_cz: *belong to* — pevná dvojice a *to* skončí na konci.

items.en: Here is the report you asked for.
items.cz: Tady je ta zpráva, o kterou jsi žádal.
items.gap: Here is the report you asked ____.
accepts: Here is the report you asked for.
items.explanation: *ask for* something. Leaving it out is the commonest slip here.
items.explanation_cz: *ask for* něco. Vynechat to je tady nejčastější chyba.

items.en: That is the friend I went to Rome with.
items.cz: To je kamarád, se kterým jsem jel do Říma.
items.gap: That is the friend I went to Rome ____.
accepts: That's the friend I went to Rome with.
That is the friend I went to Rome with.
items.explanation: *go somewhere with* someone — *with* goes right to the end.
items.explanation_cz: *go somewhere with* někým — *with* jde úplně na konec.

items.en: The man whose car was stolen called the police.
items.cz: Muž, kterému ukradli auto, zavolal policii.
items.wrong: The man which car was stolen called the police.
accepts: The man whose car was stolen called the police.
items.explanation: *Which* cannot show possession. Use **whose**, for things as well as people.
items.explanation_cz: *Which* nemůže ukazovat vlastnictví. Použij **whose**, i pro věci.

items.en: He arrived very late, which annoyed everyone.
items.cz: Přišel hodně pozdě, což všechny naštvalo.
items.wrong: He arrived very late, what annoyed everyone.
accepts: He arrived very late, which annoyed everyone.
items.explanation: Czech *což* is **which** in English, never *what*.
items.explanation_cz: České *což* je v angličtině **which**, nikdy *what*.

items.en: That is the man I told you about.
items.cz: To je ten muž, o kterém jsem ti říkal.
items.wrong: That is the man about I told you.
accepts: That's the man I told you about.
That is the man I told you about.
items.explanation: English does not put the preposition there. It goes to the **end**: *told you about*.
items.explanation_cz: Angličtina tam předložku nedává. Jde na **konec**: *told you about*.

items.en: The person to whom I spoke was very helpful.
items.cz: Člověk, se kterým jsem mluvil, byl velmi ochotný.
items.wrong: The person to who I spoke was very helpful.
accepts: The person to whom I spoke was very helpful.
items.explanation: After a preposition the form is **whom**, not *who*.
items.explanation_cz: Po předložce je tvar **whom**, ne *who*.

items.en: This is the house we used to live in.
items.cz: To je dům, ve kterém jsme bydleli.
items.wrong: This is the house we used to live.
accepts: This is the house we used to live in.
items.explanation: The preposition cannot simply vanish: *live* **in** a house.
items.explanation_cz: Předložka nemůže prostě zmizet: *live* **in** a house.

items.en: She passed the exam, which surprised nobody.
items.cz: Udělala tu zkoušku, což nikoho nepřekvapilo.
items.wrong: She passed the exam, that surprised nobody.
accepts: She passed the exam, which surprised nobody.
items.explanation: *That* can never follow a comma. A non-defining clause takes **which**.
items.explanation_cz: *That* nikdy nemůže být po čárce. Neurčující věta má **which**.
